review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the neighbouring Nonneg files (Basic, Ring, Module) to compare the simp lemma conventions. Most of the simp lemmas here (coe_inv, inv_mk, coe_div, mk_div_mk, coe_zpow, mk_zpow, coe_nnratCast, mk_nnratCast) follow the pattern in Nonneg/Basic.lean and look fine. `unitsEquivPos` uses `@[simps]` on a multiplicative equivalence, which is unremarkable. The one concern is `mk_nnqsmul`. My reading of how its statement elaborates comes from how the `•` and `=` elaborators work. I could not run Lean, so I did not confirm that the lemma is a coercion equation or that the simpNF linter flags it. The finding is therefore hedged.

findings.problem: The statement `(⟨q • a, _⟩ : Nonneg α) = q • a` has `a : α` on the right and the left side has type `Nonneg α`. I believe `•` is elaborated as `leftact%`, so `a` is a leaf of the binop tree, and the `=` elaborator then inserts a coercion on the left. If so, the lemma says `(↑⟨q • a, _⟩ : α) = q • a`, i.e. it is about `Subtype.val` applied to a constructor. That left side is reduced by projection reduction before any simp lemma is tried, so the `@[simp]` attribute is likely useless and could be flagged by the simpNF linter. The coercion case is already covered by the simp lemma `coe_nnqsmul`. The lemma the name suggests is `q • ⟨a, ha⟩ = ⟨q • a, _⟩`, which is missing from the interface. Neighbouring files do state it: `Nonneg.mk_nsmul` in Nonneg/Basic.lean and `mk_smul` in Nonneg/Module.lean both put the smul on the left and the constructor on the right. The proof is also duplicated inline in `instNNRatSMul` and here, although `nnqsmul_nonneg` in this file states exactly that fact.
findings.proposed_change:
Restate the lemma with the smul on the left and the constructor on the right. Use `nnqsmul_nonneg q ha` for the proof component, and use it in `instNNRatSMul` too:
`@[simp] lemma mk_nnqsmul (q : ℚ≥0) (a : α) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : q • (⟨a, ha⟩ : Nonneg α) = ⟨q • a, nnqsmul_nonneg q ha⟩ := rfl`.
This matches the `mk_nsmul` orientation. Equivalently, if the lemma really is a coercion equation, drop `@[simp]` since `coe_nnqsmul` already covers it.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then rewrite `q • ⟨a, ha⟩` to a constructor form, consistent with `mk_nsmul`, `mk_add_mk` and `mk_mul_mk`. This removes a simp lemma that probably never fires or trips the linter. It also removes the duplicated inline nonnegativity proof.

evidence.excerpt: (hx : 0 ≤ x) : (n • (⟨x, hx⟩ : Nonneg α)) = ⟨n • x, nsmul_nonneg hx n⟩ :=
lemma mk_smul (a) (ha) (x : S) : (⟨a, ha⟩ : R≥0) • x = a • x :=
lemma nnqsmul_nonneg (q : ℚ≥0) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : 0 ≤ q • a
